Home/IoT sensors/Radar distance sensor

Wireless radar
distance sensor.

Measure the distance. Know the level.

The Hitelecom H Series wireless radar distance sensor measures the distance to a selected surface or target without contact. Monitor water levels and bulk-material heights, or discuss a reference-target arrangement for a defined movement project. Depending on the configuration, readings are sent over 4G, NB-IoT or LoRa to Hitelecom Cloud or a compatible customer platform. Select the range, target, mounting arrangement and reporting profile for your site.

KEY FEATURES

A clear reading.
A connected operation.

See water, materials and selected positions from a distance. Match the target, installation and data connection to the work your team needs to do.

Non-contact measurement.

Measure from above the water or material surface, or along a clear path to a defined target. Plan access and mounting without an immersed sensing probe.

Remote level visibility.

Bring readings from tanks, silos and remote sites into one monitoring view. Set the distance reference and level conversion around the installation.

A range for the task.

The published H310-MW012 reference covers 0.3–12 m. Other range and installation requirements can be reviewed as project configurations.

Specified measurement performance.

The model reference lists ±1 mm accuracy under 25°C Hitelecom laboratory conditions and 1 mm reading resolution. Select performance around the target and site geometry.

Protected wireless housing.

IP68 enclosure protection is listed for the model reference. Match the mounting, exposed sensing face and access for maintenance to the environment.

A wireless path for your site.

Choose a 4G, NB-IoT or LoRa configuration around the local network and integration path. Agree sampling, reporting and alert requirements together.

Local setup & remote updates.

NFC configuration and remote OTA firmware updates are listed in the published product information. Confirm the setup method and update workflow for the supplied configuration.

Platform-ready readings.

Associate distance and derived level with a device, vessel or site record. Agree the units, measurement reference, timestamps and payload with your platform team.

FROM DISTANCE TO LEVEL

One distance reading.
A useful site reference.

For a vertical, fixed top-mounted installation, level equals the reference height minus the distance to the surface. Define the reference in the same unit and validate it on site.

LevelL = H − D

4.2 m = 6.0 m − 1.8 m

Illustrative example · fixed top-mounted sensor

Distance

The directly measured gap along the selected measuring path.

Level

A height relative to a defined datum. For the illustrated vertical installation: L = H − D.

Volume & flow

Volume uses vessel geometry or a tank table. Flow uses an appropriate structure or site-specific relationship. Agree these calculations with the platform team.

FROM DISTANCE TO TARGET MOVEMENT

A defined target.
An independent reference.

For movement observations against an independent reference, compare the distance to the same target at each observation. The reference stays independent of the movement being assessed; the measurement axis defines which component of movement is observed.

ΔD = D(t) − D₀Change in distance along the measuring axis

Specify the change your engineer needs to resolve, then verify target return, repeatability, temperature effects and reference stability at the site. A vertical settlement interpretation requires a vertical measuring arrangement or separately validated survey geometry.

For joint or bearing-gap observations, the mounting member is the relative reference. Absolute movement requires a separate stable survey reference.

MOUNTING & COMMISSIONING

A stable reference.
A clear view of the target.

Use a rigid, accessible mounting point and a clear path to the intended surface or target. Check the complete distance span, target size and alignment, nearby structures, fill streams and environmental conditions. For movement projects, establish an independent reference and baseline, then verify repeatability against the required change. Commission the reading and reference together.

FROM A READING TO A RESPONSE

Measure. Report.
Keep teams informed.

Sampling is when the sensor measures. Reporting is when the reading reaches the platform. Define both around how quickly the level or target can change, then agree the alert and response workflow.

01

Measure

The selected radar configuration reads the distance to the intended target. Choose the sampling schedule and verify the reference against the installation.

02

Report

The chosen cellular or LoRa configuration carries readings through the agreed network path. Match scheduled reporting and configured alerts to the operational need.

03

Review & respond

Review distance, derived level and trends in the connected platform. Define thresholds, recipients and the next action for your operations team.

POWER & REPORTING PROFILELong-life monitoring.
Matched to the task.

The current H Series datasheet gives a battery-life reference of more than 10 years with scheduled reporting every four hours. The 19,000 mAh battery is the H300 reference configuration. Actual service life depends on the supplied battery, measurement activity, transmissions, network conditions and temperature. Specify faster-changing applications with their required update and response times.

01Manholes, drains & sediment checks6 applications +

Observe water levels and exposed sediment surfaces at defined drainage points. A documented datum or clean-pit baseline gives each reading meaning, while chamber geometry, surface condition and maintenance timing guide the project selection. Compare the trends with rainfall and inspection records to plan the next visit.

Sewer manhole water levels

Surface-level selectionSee rising water before scheduling the next inspection.+

Measure the distance to the water surface in a selected sewer manhole and relate it to the chamber’s surveyed level reference. The resulting trend helps drainage teams review surcharge, rainfall response and how quickly the level returns after an event. Choose a fixed upper mounting position with a clear view past ladders and pipework, then assess condensation, foam and the expected high-water condition. An unusual level provides a reason for targeted inspection; identifying the cause and position of a pipe blockage requires the wider drainage investigation.

What is measured
Distance to the water surface; chamber water level relative to a surveyed datum.
Installation point
A fixed upper-chamber bracket above the observation surface, with a clear path past access fittings.
Project requirements
Chamber dimensions, low and high water levels, flood exposure, surface conditions, site classification, signal coverage and observation interval.
Discuss this application ↗

Exposed sediment in dry catchpits

Surface-level selectionGive exposed sediment a repeatable clean-pit reference.+

Measure the distance to an exposed sediment surface when a catchpit is dry or drawn down sufficiently to reveal the deposit. A fixed mounting height and a recorded clean-pit baseline allow the local deposit height to be compared over time. This can help maintenance teams prioritise inspection and cleaning at the observed point. Select a broad, representative patch away from inlet jets and assess the return signal as the surface changes. During standing-water periods, interpret the observed surface accordingly; submerged sediment thickness is a separate measurement task.

What is measured
Distance to exposed sediment; local deposit height from the clean-pit baseline.
Installation point
A fixed upper bracket facing a broad, exposed deposit patch away from side openings.
Project requirements
Clean-pit survey, expected deposit profile, dry observation windows, minimum distance, pipe openings and maintenance access.
Discuss this application ↗

Roadside gully sediment height

Surface-level selectionPlan gully cleaning around the surface you can observe.+

Observe the exposed sand or silt bed inside a roadside gully during suitable low-water or dry periods. Relate the distance to a fixed chamber reference and the surveyed clean floor to follow local accumulation between maintenance visits. The trend can support cleaning priorities when combined with the gully’s rainfall response and inspection records. Keep the measuring path clear of the grate and surrounding metalwork, and select a model whose minimum distance fits the chamber. Document whether each observation represents exposed deposits or a covering water surface.

What is measured
Distance to the exposed gully deposit surface; local height above the clean floor.
Installation point
An approved protected bracket beneath the access frame, clear of grate bars and the selected surface.
Project requirements
Chamber depth, grate clearance, clean-floor baseline, standing-water pattern, traffic protection and service access.
Discuss this application ↗

Culvert upstream water levels

Surface-level selectionFollow the water backing up before the culvert.+

Measure the upstream water surface at a fixed point beside a culvert inlet. A surveyed headwall or bank-mounted bracket connects each distance reading to the site’s water-level datum. The trend helps the drainage team compare rainfall response, drawdown and conditions before an inspection or cleaning visit. Place the observation area away from inlet turbulence, floating debris and passing traffic, with sufficient clearance across the full stage range. Compare upstream readings with downstream levels and site observations to understand a change in drainage performance and plan the next investigation.

What is measured
Distance to upstream water; stage relative to the culvert-site datum.
Installation point
A surveyed fixed arm over open upstream water, outside the flow entrance and traffic envelope.
Project requirements
Lowest and highest stage, inlet geometry, debris exposure, downstream context, mounting stability and reporting timing.
Discuss this application ↗

Upstream and downstream level trends

Surface-level selectionCompare two observation points on the same drainage reach.+

Use separate radar observations at approved upstream and downstream points to follow the water-level relationship across a selected drainage reach. Survey both mounting references to a common datum and compare time-aligned readings with rainfall, pumping and inspection records. A changing difference can help the operator decide where to investigate drainage performance or arrange maintenance. Select representative surfaces at both points, check local turbulence and record the conditions around each observation. The interpretation belongs to the site’s hydraulic and maintenance assessment, supported by the paired measurements and wider operating context.

What is measured
Water levels at two defined points; their time-aligned difference on a common datum.
Installation point
One fixed bracket per observation point, each surveyed to the same vertical reference.
Project requirements
Two-site survey, connecting reach geometry, timestamps, pump or rain records, surface conditions and matched sampling profiles.
Discuss this application ↗

Pump-station wet wells

Surface-level selectionUnderstand the wet-well cycle between service visits.+

Measure the wastewater surface inside a lift-station wet well from an approved upper mounting position. These observations can support service planning, operating-profile review and comparison between stations. Distance to the wastewater surface; wet-well level relative to the chamber datum.
Installation point

Project requirements

The project trial assesses target return, mounting temperature and repeatability under the expected operating conditions, while the engineering team determines how this selected-point observation contributes to its foundation inspection and maintenance programme.

What is measured
Target-to-reference distance and its baseline change at one foundation point.
Installation point
An independent benchmark-mounted bracket viewing the foundation target across a clear vertical gap.
Project requirements
Independent-reference verification, target attachment, foundation drawing, expected movement, machine states, environmental trial and required observation interval.

ANSWERS FOR YOUR PROJECT

Frequently
asked questions.

Answers on surface levels, manhole maintenance, reference-target projects and the information needed for a suitable configuration.

Ask about your project ↗
What does a wireless radar distance sensor measure?+

A radar distance sensor uses reflected radio signals to measure the distance from its measurement reference to a target surface. The Hitelecom H Series sends readings for remote monitoring. With an agreed reference and installation, distance data can support water level, tank level, bulk-material level or changes in target position.

How do I choose the range and measurement performance?+

Use the nearest and farthest target positions to define the required range. The published H310-MW012 reference specifies 0.3–12 m, ±1 mm accuracy under 25°C Hitelecom laboratory conditions, and a 1 mm reading resolution. Share the target material and installation geometry so Hitelecom can review the appropriate configuration, including requests for other ranges.

How is a distance reading converted into level or inventory?+

For a fixed sensor mounted vertically above the surface, level is calculated from the configured reference height minus the measured distance to the surface. Volume uses the vessel geometry or a calibrated tank table. For bulk solids, the mounting position and surface profile also matter; a local level reading supports inventory planning when interpreted with the agreed vessel and material information.

Can radar distance monitoring be used for liquids and bulk solids?+

Radar is used for liquid surfaces and for bulk materials such as grain, pellets and aggregates. Selection depends on the material, surface conditions, vessel shape and accessible mounting position. Share the medium, filling method and expected environment with Hitelecom to review a suitable configuration for your tank, silo, hopper or open-water site.

How can manhole level data support sediment and blockage checks?+

A fixed radar above a sewer or drain chamber observes the exposed water surface. Water-level trends, compared with rainfall, pumping and downstream conditions, can help the maintenance team select locations for inspection. Where the chamber is dry or emptied and the deposit surface is exposed, its local height can be assessed against a known chamber datum after confirming the target return.

Specify whether you need water level, exposed deposit height or a submerged sludge interface. The submerged interface is a separate measurement task requiring an appropriate instrument; water-surface distance alone does not identify the amount or location of a pipe blockage.

How are distance changes used in structural movement projects?+

A defined target can be observed from an independent, stable reference. The difference between the current gap and its baseline is a relative change along the measuring axis. For a settlement interpretation, establish a vertical measuring arrangement or validated survey geometry, with periodic checks of the reference.

Specify the required observable change and monitoring interval, then review target size, alignment, environmental effects and on-site repeatability with the project engineer. These are proposed selection briefs: the published H310-MW012 laboratory distance accuracy is a model reference, rather than a validated field settlement performance specification.

For a joint or bearing gap, the mounting member and opposing target define a relative opening. Independent survey information is needed when the project also requires absolute movement.

What is the difference between radar and ultrasonic level measurement?+

Radar uses electromagnetic waves; ultrasonic measurement uses sound waves. Air temperature changes the speed of sound used in ultrasonic measurement; radar does not depend on sound speed. Their response to changing air conditions, dust, vapour and surface conditions differs. Both need an appropriate measuring path and installation. Choose by the medium, required range, available mounting space and site conditions; for foam, condensation or deposits, include those details in the application review.

Where should a non-contact radar distance sensor be installed?+

Use a rigid mounting point with a clear measuring path to the intended surface or target. For level monitoring, plan the mounting position around the vessel shape, fill stream and internal structures, and keep the full operating range within the selected configuration. Establish the measurement reference and verify readings at representative levels during commissioning.

How are wireless connectivity and reporting configured?+

The H Series offers H200 with LoRa, H300 with 4G LTE and H500 with NB-IoT, selected by configuration. Match the network to site coverage and the destination platform, then define sampling, scheduled reporting and alert requirements. The current H Series datasheet gives a battery-life reference of more than 10 years with scheduled reporting every four hours; the 19,000 mAh battery is the H300 reference configuration. Actual service life depends on the supplied battery, measurement activity, transmissions, network conditions and temperature.

What information should I provide for a radar distance sensor quotation?+

Send the application, target material, minimum and maximum measuring distances, mounting position and approximate quantity. A site photo or vessel drawing helps define the measuring path. Include ambient and process conditions, the required reading and reporting intervals, wireless coverage, platform requirements and the level or distance events you want to monitor.
